name: Playing Preschool Year 1 by Busy Toddler

principles: Play-based learning — hands-on activities over worksheets or drilling
Background knowledge over mastery — exposure and experience, not testing
Spiral skill development — revisit same 7 skills with increasing complexity across 19 units
Routine as scaffold — predictable weekly rotation (M: predicting+sorting, T: letter+numbers, W: predicting+measuring, Th: letter+numbers, F: recall+shapes/letter review) gives parent confidence
Rigid flexibility — strong routine but moldable to fit the family's day and child's pace
Read alouds as anchor — every day starts with a themed book; reading comprehension is built through questions, predictions, and retelling

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Play-Based Preschool (Busy Toddler model)
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: Hands-on, theme-driven preschool with no mastery expectations. Spiral skill development across 7 core skills (predicting, recall/retell, sorting, number sense, measuring, shapes, alphabet). Background knowledge and positive associations with learning are the goals. 45-60 minutes/day.

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Playing Preschool Weekly Format
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: 5 days/week, 2-week themed units. Fixed skill rotation: Mon=predicting+sorting, Tue=letter+numbers, Wed=predicting+measuring, Thu=letter+numbers, Fri=recall/retell+shapes (wk1) or letter review (wk2). 4 activities/day: opening, read aloud, learning activity, easy activity. Sensory bins, process art, STEM, gross/fine motor woven throughout.

mappings.curriculumTopic: Making predictions about stories (cover, during, after)
mappings.notes: Homa has 'Predicting what happens next' — partial match. Playing Preschool treats predicting more broadly (also science/math predictions, not just story)

mappings.curriculumTopic: Retelling stories in sequence, recalling facts from themes
mappings.notes: Homa has 'Characters, settings, and events' and comprehension topics but no dedicated 'retelling' topic for preschool

mappings.curriculumTopic: Sort and classify by color, size, shape, texture, multiple attributes
mappings.notes: Maps to 'Sorting into categories' in Data & Statistics

mappings.curriculumTopic: Counting 1-5 (five frames), growing to 1-10 (ten frames), numeral recognition, 1:1 correspondence, quantity, comparing, intro addition concepts
mappings.notes: Strong overlap — 'One More Each Time', 'Comparing groups: more or fewer', 'How Many in Total?' all match

mappings.curriculumTopic: Comparing size, length, height, weight, capacity (not units)
mappings.notes: Maps to 'Comparing Lengths & Heights', 'Comparing Capacity' in Measurement

mappings.curriculumTopic: Circle, square, triangle identification; attributes (sides, points); shapes in the real world; spatial awareness
mappings.notes: Maps to '2-D shapes', 'Positional Language' in Geometry

mappings.curriculumTopic: Letter recognition (upper + lower), letter sounds, letters not in alphabetical order, letter hunts, alphabet portfolio art
mappings.notes: Maps to 'Knowing all letters' and 'Blending Sounds to Read Words' (early). Non-alphabetical order is a pedagogical choice, not a taxonomy gap

mappings.curriculumTopic: Process art, crafts, apple stamping, finger painting, construction paper projects
mappings.notes: Homa has 'Art Appreciation' under English/Fine Arts but no process art or craft-making topics. Art is treated as a standalone subject in this curriculum

mappings.curriculumTopic: Color mixing, dissolving/evaporating, sink/float, ramp rolling, plant growth, life cycles, weather observation
mappings.notes: Broad coverage — maps across Matter & Materials, Organisms & Life Processes, Weather & Climate, Forces & Motion, Earth's Systems

mappings.curriculumTopic: Sensory bins (rice, cornmeal, applesauce, water), tactile exploration
Tongs transfer, toothpick poking, threading, dot sticker work, cutting
Running to colors, apple hunts, jumping, obstacle courses
Days of the week, months, weather, counting on, ordinal numbers
mappings.notes: Maps to 'Time Concepts', 'Weather Recognition', 'Daily Routine Building' in Daily Living

mappings.curriculumTopic: Pretend play, acting out books, dress-up (community helpers unit)
Unit-specific songs and poems for phonemic awareness and memory
mappings.notes: Phonemic awareness is in Phonics & Word Reading. Poetry/music as a teaching modality is not explicitly captured

sessionLengthMinutes.notes: Can be broken across the day — doesn't need to be one block

layer3_structure.weeklyTemplate: Monday: predicting + sorting. Tuesday: letter name + numbers. Wednesday: predicting + measuring. Thursday: letter name + numbers. Friday (wk1): recall/retell + shapes. Friday (wk2): recall/retell + letter review.
layer3_structure.dailyRoutine: Opening (morning calendar + song/poem) → Introduce/review topic → Read aloud → Things to talk about → Learning activity → Easy activity. Extensions sprinkled throughout.
layer3_structure.reviewRhythm: Weekly Friday review (shapes wk1, letter review wk2). Skills spiral from Unit 1 through Unit 19 with increasing complexity.
layer3_structure.letterSequence: Aa, Rr, Nn, Cc+Jj, Mm, Ss, Bb, Qq+Uu, Hh, Tt, Ff, Ww+Kk, Ee, Pp+Ll, Yy+Zz, Dd, Oo+Xx, Gg+Vv, Ii
layer3_structure.letterOrderRationale: Non-alphabetical by design. Easy letters (same upper/lower like Cc, Jj) doubled up. Tricky letters (different upper/lower like Ee, Aa) taught alone. Some letters match theme (Tt for Transportation).

activityTypes.description: Sort real objects (apples, toys, household items) by color, size, shape, texture, or multiple attributes onto construction paper or into baskets

suggestedRecipe.name: sorting-mat
suggestedRecipe.description: Printable sorting mat with labeled category zones (2-4 columns or T-chart) plus either cut-out images to sort OR blank space for physical objects. For play-based curricula, the mat defines the categories while the child uses real household items.

activityTypes.notes: Most sorting in this curriculum uses real objects, not printables. The recipe would be supplementary — a printable mat to organize the sort.

activityTypes.description: Tape or drawn frames for counting objects 1-5 (early) growing to 1-10 (later). Used with real objects placed in frames.
activityTypes.notes: Could adapt counting-mat recipe. But PP uses physical frames taped on floor — the printable version would be a supplement.

activityTypes.description: Storage container filled with rice, cornmeal, water, applesauce, etc. Child explores with scoops, tongs, cups. Themed additions (food coloring, small objects to find).

suggestedRecipe.name: sensory-bin-card
suggestedRecipe.description: Printable setup card with a title, materials list, suggested play prompts, and learning connections. Not the activity itself — the guide to setting it up. Could include vocabulary words to use during play.

activityTypes.notes: Sensory bins are inherently physical — no printable replaces them. But a setup/prompt card helps the parent run them well.

activityTypes.description: One letter-themed art page per letter (26 total). Child decorates the letter shape, cuts it out, glues to construction paper. Builds into an alphabet book keepsake.

suggestedRecipe.name: alphabet-art-page
suggestedRecipe.description: Large outlined letter (both upper and lower case) designed for decorating — big enough for dot stickers, paint, gluing materials. Bottom of page has a few themed images starting with that letter. Print-friendly B&W.

activityTypes.description: Themed book read daily with guided prediction questions, vocabulary discussion, and comprehension checks. Books read twice per week for deeper learning.

suggestedRecipe.name: read-aloud-companion
suggestedRecipe.description: Printable companion card for a read-aloud: book title, prediction prompts (before/during/after), vocabulary words to emphasize, discussion questions, and a retelling prompt. One page per book.

activityTypes.description: Find a specific letter in books, pantry items, around the house, with flashlights, on sticky notes. Varied environments for the same hunt.

suggestedRecipe.name: letter-hunt-card
suggestedRecipe.description: Printable hunt checklist: target letter (large, upper+lower), hunt locations (books, pantry, signs, etc.), tally marks for found letters, space to write/draw words starting with that letter.

activityTypes.description: Open-ended art: finger painting, apple stamping, construction paper collages, painting sunshine, making freight trains from colored boxes. Product is secondary to the process.
activityTypes.notes: Coloring page recipe covers some of this. But process art is often freeform — no printable needed, just supplies.

activityTypes.description: Running to colors, apple hide-and-seek hunts, building obstacle courses, book dominoes, jumping activities.

suggestedRecipe.name: activity-card
suggestedRecipe.description: Simple activity instruction card: title, materials, setup steps, play variations, learning connections. For physical activities that need a parent guide, not a worksheet.

activityTypes.description: Transfer with tongs/ladles/forks, poking with golf tees, threading, peeling/placing dot stickers, cutting.
activityTypes.notes: Purely physical — no printable. An activity-card recipe would cover the guide aspect.

activityTypes.description: Color mixing in bags/water, dissolving substances, rain cloud in a glass, rolling apples down ramps, freezing/melting ice. Hands-on with real materials.

suggestedRecipe.name: experiment-card
suggestedRecipe.description: Printable experiment card: title, hypothesis prompt, materials, steps with illustrations, observation space, 'what happened?' recording area. Kid-friendly science method without the jargon.

activityTypes.description: Daily opening: discuss date, day of the week, month, weather. Sing calendar songs (days, months, weather song). 2-minute routine.
activityTypes.notes: Visual schedule / daily rhythm cards in taste model are related. A printable calendar routine board could work.

activityTypes.description: Acting out stories, pretend jobs (community helpers), building themed play environments (freight train from boxes).
activityTypes.notes: Inherently physical/imaginative. A prompt card or role-play scenario card could support it.

notes: This is a full 38-week, 190-day preschool program targeting ages 2.5-5. It's fundamentally different from the worksheet/printable-heavy references we've ingested so far — it's almost entirely hands-on with real objects. The printable needs are minimal (alphabet portfolio pages, maybe setup cards). The biggest value for Homa is learning the STRUCTURE: the weekly rotation pattern, the spiral skill model, and the daily routine sequence. This teaches Homa's curriculum writer how to plan play-based preschool weeks. Very strong overlap with existing taxonomy in math and ELA. The unmapped areas (sensory, motor skills, dramatic play) are physical development domains that many preschool curricula share.
